meta.name: Septic Shock — Urosepsis with Steroid-Dependent Adrenal Suppression

patient.name: Ruth Callahan
patient.chiefComplaint: Confusion and weakness, nursing home staff report two days of dysuria

history.hpi: Nursing home staff report the patient has complained of burning with urination and foul-smelling urine for the past two days. This morning she was found unusually drowsy and difficult to arouse for breakfast, with a documented temperature of 102.4°F on the facility's routine check. Staff called EMS when she became difficult to keep awake.
pastMedical: Mild dementia (baseline oriented to person only)
history.lastOralIntake: Sips of water this morning, refused breakfast
history.events: Facility nursing staff called 911 after the patient became increasingly difficult to arouse over the past hour

scene.dispatch: 83-year-old female, altered mental status, skilled nursing facility
scene.location: Skilled nursing facility, semi-private room, patient supine in bed
scene.bystanders: Charge nurse present with medication administration record and vital signs log
visualCues: Patient lying in bed, eyes closed, rousable only to sternal rub
Skin flushed and warm despite reported chills overnight per nursing notes
Foley catheter in place with cloudy, dark amber urine
Facility vitals log shows temperature trending up over the past 12 hours
Medication administration record shows daily prednisone 10 mg

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find an 83-year-old female with altered mental status, rousable only to sternal rub, febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive. A Foley catheter is in place draining cloudy urine.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and rapid, flash capillary refill under 1 second
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to sternal rub, no focal deficit noted
otherFindings: Foley catheter draining cloudy, dark amber urine
Facility temperature log shows fever trending up overnight
No neck stiffness or rash noted

transitions.condition: Crew checks blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a cause of AMS, establishes IV access, and begins a pressure-infused isotonic fluid bolus toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg.

phases.name: BGL checked, IV fluids started
phases.description: Crew rules out hypoglycemia, establishes IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation for distributive shock from suspected urosepsis. The medication administration record shows daily prednisone, flagging a risk of adrenal suppression if shock persists despite fluids.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming a normal blood glucose, the crew establishes IV access and begins rapid isotonic fluid boluses targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg, while noting the patient's chronic steroid dependence from the medication administration record.

otherFindings: 18-gauge IV established in the right forearm
500 mL isotonic bolus infusing under pressure
Prednisone 10 mg daily confirmed on medication administration record

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose; correct if less than 60 mg/dL (result 118 mg/dL, no correction needed)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood sugar, and correct if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a rapidly reversible cause of AMS that must be excluded early.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access; begin 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus, pressure infused over less than 15 min toward MAP 65 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle. IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each ... Physiologic target: MAP goal 65 mmHg. Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved
expectedActions.rationale: Early, aggressive fluid resuscitation is essential in suspected septic shock.

expectedActions.shortAction: Identify chronic steroid dependence (prednisone 10 mg daily) as an adrenal suppression risk factor
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: History of GI bleeding ... Adrenal insufficiency ... Presence of a central line or port
expectedActions.rationale: Chronic steroid use predisposes to relative adrenal insufficiency, which can worsen fluid-refractory shock if unrecognized.

transitions.condition: Despite an initial fluid bolus, the patient remains hypotensive. Given her known long-term steroid dependence, the crew administers hydrocortisone rather than proceeding straight to a vasopressor.
The crew focuses only on fluid resuscitation and does not review the medication administration record, missing the patient's chronic steroid dependence and the indication for hydrocortisone.

phases.name: Fluid-refractory shock, hydrocortisone given
phases.description: The patient remains hypotensive after the initial fluid bolus. Recognizing her chronic steroid dependence, the crew administers hydrocortisone while continuing fluid resuscitation and preparing for a possible vasopressor if the blood pressure does not improve.
phases.triggerCondition: After the first 500 mL bolus, blood pressure remains low. Because the patient is on chronic daily prednisone, the crew treats this as fluid-refractory shock with a possible component of relative adrenal insufficiency and gives IV hydrocortisone per protocol.

otherFindings: Advanced notification given to receiving hospital

expectedActions.shortAction: Hydrocortisone succinate 100 mg IV (58 kg × 2 mg/kg = 116 mg → cap at 100 mg max)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If there is a history of adrenal insufficiency, long-term steroid dependence, or fluid-refractory shock requiring vasopressors give: Hydrocortisone succinate, 2 mg/kg (maximum 100 mg) IV/IM (preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Chronic steroid use can suppress the adrenal axis, blunting the physiologic stress response and worsening shock unless stress-dose steroid is given.

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advanced notification to receiving hospital of suspected septic shock
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide advanced notification to the hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the hospital to prepare sepsis resources (labs, antibiotics, possible ICU bed) before arrival.

transitions.condition: Following hydrocortisone and continued fluid resuscitation, blood pressure and mental status trend toward baseline; crew continues reassessment en route.

phases.name: Perfusion improves, transport continues
phases.description: With fluids and hydrocortisone on board, the patient's perfusion and mental status trend toward baseline. The crew continues serial reassessment and transports for definitive urosepsis workup and antibiotics.
phases.triggerCondition: After hydrocortisone and ongoing fluid resuscitation, vital signs and mental status improve; crew continues serial reassessment en route to the hospital.

otherFindings: Mental status trending toward baseline (oriented to person)
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I think I'm feeling a little better."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess full vital signs and neurologic status at least every 15 minutes en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Septic patients can deteriorate again even after initial improvement.

phases.name: Steroid history not identified
phases.description: The crew continues fluid boluses without reviewing the medication administration record, missing the patient's chronic prednisone use. Blood pressure remains persistently low despite two fluid boluses, and the crew must escalate to a vasopressor without the benefit of stress-dose steroid coverage.
phases.triggerCondition: The medication administration record is not reviewed, so the chronic steroid dependence goes unrecognized; after two fluid boluses the patient remains hypotensive and requires vasopressor support.

otherFindings: Two isotonic boluses given, blood pressure persistently low
Medication administration record not yet reviewed

expectedActions.shortAction: Review medication administration record; identify prednisone use and give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV alongside norepinephrine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If there is a history of adrenal insufficiency, long-term steroid dependence, or fluid-refractory shock requiring vasopressors give: Hydrocortisone succinate, 2 mg/kg (maximum 100 mg) IV/IM (preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Vasopressor-refractory shock in a steroid-dependent patient should prompt stress-dose steroid administration, not vasopressors alone.
